claims.claim: After Domri Rade's death, official sources present the Gruul Clans as lacking a single uncontested formal leader. By 2024, Wizards describes the Gruul as generally following Borborygmos, leader of the Burning-Tree Clan, while identifying Nikya and the Zhur-Taa Clan as the only real potential challenge to his power.
claims.notes: This is a negative finding from reviewed sources, not proof that no later canon exists.
claims.risk_of_hallucination_or_overreach: Low if kept to this atomic wording.

claims.claim: A placement model can interpret Gruul as strongly anti-institutional and freedom-oriented because official sources repeatedly emphasize anti-civilization beliefs, clan looseness, rioting, and resistance to encroachment.
claims.risk_of_hallucination_or_overreach: Medium if presented as official psychology rather than placement interpretation.

claims.claim: A placement model can interpret Gruul as valuing embodied strength and direct action over formal authority because official sources emphasize strongest-rule leadership, warfare, bloodrush, riot, and Domri's combat-based rise.
claims.risk_of_hallucination_or_overreach: Medium if reduced to simple aggression without the ecological grievance context.

claims.claim: A placement model can interpret Gruul's nature-protection impulse as a sanctity-of-the-wild signal because official sources frame the guild as former stewards of wild places reacting to the destruction of wilderness and sacred groves.
claims.risk_of_hallucination_or_overreach: Medium if treated as Wizards-authored Moral Foundations Theory rather than an external analytical model.

claims.claim: A placement model can treat love of bureaucracy, deference to title-based authority, and comfort with urban expansion as poor-fit indicators for Gruul because official sources emphasize anti-civilization, strength-based leadership, and conflict with encroaching guilds.
claims.risk_of_hallucination_or_overreach: Low if phrased as matching heuristic rather than moral judgment.

claims.claim: In the repository archive story 'Gruul Ingenuity,' Nikya of the Old Ways is Kal's clan leader and sends him to watch Izzet activity near Zhur-Taa territory.

claims.claim: In 'Gruul Ingenuity,' Nikya invokes Gruul law and right to claim bloodcrime and seek vengeance after blood is spilled, innocents are slaughtered, and territory is defiled.
claims.notes: Supports territorial justice/vengeance framing.
claims.risk_of_hallucination_or_overreach: Medium if treated as codified law for every clan.

claims.risk_of_hallucination_or_overreach: Medium; do not generalize into permanent faction policy.

claims.claim: In 'Gruul Ingenuity,' Nikya chooses her war-party by touching upheld weapons, a practice the narration says clan leaders have used for thousands of years.

claims.claim: In 'Rage of the Unsung,' Ruric and Thar are treated as Ghor Clan chieftains, and Dryzek ultimately pledges loyalty to them.

claims.claim: In 'Rage of the Unsung,' Gruul Rage spreads from one Gruul to another during a destructive tribute to the Raze-Boar, with tattoos and eyes shining as the emotion passes.

claims.claim: In 'Rage of the Unsung,' Arrus frames the Gruul fight as not only destruction but also as curing Ravnica of gratuitous construction and institutional corruption.

claims.claim: Arrus is a Ghor Clan viashino tattoo artist and narrator in 'Rage of the Unsung' who is cast out as clanless and later rallies others around the Rubblebelt threat.

claims.claim: A placement model can treat Gruul Rage as protective and ecological anger rather than only generalized aggression, because story evidence ties Rage to the dying Rubblebelt, land-draining magic, and erased stories.

claims.claim: A placement model can represent Gruul contribution as broader than front-line brawling because Kal, Arrus, and Baas contribute through scouting, magic, tattoo-art, shamanic practice, or rallying as well as combat.
